climate.overview_html: Copernicus C3S confirmed September 2026 as the second-warmest September on record — 16.27°C global mean, 1.63°C above pre-industrial — with the Niño 3.4 region setting an all-time monthly sea-surface-temperature record; Carbon Brief described the 2026 Super El Niño as having reached a “remarkable” all-time record anomaly of +3.34°C, with Copernicus director Carlo Buontempo saying 2026 “could still become the hottest year on record.” IPCC-65 concluded its final day in Addis Ababa on 16 October with the AR7 delivery-timeline still unresolved across six consecutive plenaries without agreement; a formal outcome had not been published at digest compilation. In European carbon markets, EU allowances peaked at €88.3 per tonne on 12 October — the highest since late January — ahead of the 15–16 October EU Council where Italy and Czechia sought ETS reform and ETS2 delay. With COP31 (Antalya, 9–20 November) five weeks away, the EU doubled down on its emissions-cuts position after the UN flagged near-certain breach of the 1.5°C threshold.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S September 2026 Bulletin: Second-Warmest September on Record (16.27°C, 1.63°C Above Pre-Industrial); Niño 3.4 Sets All-Time Monthly SST Record; Extra-Polar Ocean Reaches Record 21.05°C; Antarctic Sea Ice Third-Lowest Winter Maximum
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service October 2026 monthly bulletin confirmed September 2026 as the second-warmest September in the ERA5 record, trailing only September 2023 by 0.11°C. The global mean surface air temperature of 16.27°C was 0.82°C above the 1991–2020 mean and 1.63°C above the pre-industrial (1850–1900) baseline — the second consecutive month exceeding 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. The Niño 3.4 region in the central equatorial Pacific set an all-time monthly SST record for September, exceeding the peaks of the 2015–16 event. The extra-polar ocean average (60°S–60°N) reached 21.05°C, the highest recorded value for any September. Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest winter maximum extent. Western Europe tied its warmest September on record; dry conditions intensified across Iberia, France, Italy, the western Balkans and Greece. Copernicus director Carlo Buontempo cautioned it is still 'too early to say' whether 2026 represents the strongest El Niño ever observed.

items.headline: Carbon Brief Analysis: 2026 Super El Niño Reaches “Remarkable” All-Time SST Record (+3.34°C Niño 3.4 Anomaly); Copernicus Director Says 2026 Could Still Become Hottest Year; Berkeley Earth Puts Probability at 93%
items.summary: Carbon Brief's October 13 analysis reported the 2026 El Niño has reached a 'remarkable' all-time record for Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately +3.34°C, exceeding the peaks of the 2015–16 event and all previous strong El Niños in the instrumental record. Copernicus director Carlo Buontempo stated 2026 could become the hottest year on record, though the final outcome hinges on October–December conditions. A separate Berkeley Earth assessment (August 2026) placed the probability of 2026 becoming the hottest year at 93%, with the likely annual mean falling between 1.536 and 1.642°C above the 1850–1900 baseline. Carbon Brief noted that El Niño's surface temperature signal typically lags the SST peak by 3–6 months, meaning its largest global temperature impact is projected for early 2027 — with 2027 itself projected at approximately 1.7°C above pre-industrial levels, a figure that would represent the most sustained exceedance of the 1.5°C Paris threshold to date.

items.headline: IPCC-65 Final Day in Addis Ababa: AR7 Delivery Timeline Unresolved Across Sixth Consecutive Plenary; Chair Skea’s September 2028 Completion Proposal Contested by India-Led Bloc; No Formal Outcome at Digest Compilation
items.summary: IPCC-65, running October 12–16 at the UN Economic Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa, reached its final day on October 16 with the Seventh Assessment Report delivery-timeline still unresolved — the sixth consecutive plenary to fail to agree the schedule. The core dispute: the EU, UK, small island states and most developed countries support IPCC Chair Jim Skea's proposal to approve all three Working Group reports by September 2028, ahead of the second Global Stocktake; India and several major emerging economies insist WG2 and WG3 must be deferred to 2029. Carbon Brief, the Earth Negotiations Bulletin and Climate Analytics have each described Addis Ababa as likely the last session at which a timeline compatible with the 2028 Stocktake could be agreed. A formal outcome had not been published as of this digest's compilation, and Carbon Brief noted that even if agreement were reached it would need to be formally approved in closing plenary.

items.headline: EU Allowances Peak at €88.3/Tonne (12 Oct) — Highest Since January; EU Council 15–16 Oct Debates ETS Reform; Italy and Czechia Push ETS2 Delay; ETS2 Market Stability Reserve Brake Gets Final Approval
items.summary: EU Emissions Trading System allowances (EUAs) rose to €88.3/tonne on October 12 — the highest level since late January 2026 — driven by buying ahead of the EU Council meeting on October 15–16. Italy and Czechia are leading calls to limit Market Stability Reserve withdrawals under the ETS and to delay the planned 2028 launch of ETS2 (which covers road transport and building heating fuels). The European Commission says ETS2 will launch January 2028 as planned; changing this requires primary legislation. The EU Parliament separately approved a Market Stability Reserve amendment for ETS2 that introduces a price-brake mechanism to limit bill impacts at launch, with the regulation to enter force 20 days after Official Journal publication. By October 15, EUAs had eased to €86.72/tonne. Analysts at Enerdata revised their 2026 annual EUA price forecast to €79.97/tonne and still project allowances above €100/tonne before 2030.

items.headline: EU Doubles Down on COP31 Emissions-Cuts Position After UN Flags Near-Certain 1.5°C Breach; Demands Extended Mitigation Work Programme to 2040 and Progress on New Climate Finance Goal Ahead of 9–20 November Antalya Summit
items.summary: The EU has reinforced its COP31 negotiating priorities following the UN Environment Programme's annual Emissions Gap Report, which found existing nationally determined contributions place the world on a roughly 3°C pathway and that a 1.5°C outcome is now unlikely without immediate, drastic acceleration. The EU's top COP31 asks: (1) extending the Mitigation Work Programme beyond 2030 to at least 2040 to maintain pressure between Global Stocktakes; (2) delivering the New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance, replacing the expired $100 billion/year pledge; (3) advancing operationalisation of Article 6 carbon market rules agreed at COP26. The EU-Australia joint COP31 co-presidency has framed the Antalya summit (November 9–20) as an 'implementation COP,' though the gap between existing pledges and 1.5°C trajectories makes significant new commitments unavoidable if the temperature goal is to be kept in play.

major_events.name: Hurricane Trudy (Eastern Pacific) — Rapidly Intensifying; Major Hurricane Forecast by Tonight; Landfall Near Manzanillo, Colima/Jalisco, This Weekend
major_events.status: As of 16 Oct: sustained winds ~90 mph (~78 kt), approximately 285 miles SW of Acapulco, moving WNW; NHC forecasts rapid intensification to major hurricane (Cat 3+) by Friday evening 16 Oct; expected landfall near Manzanillo, Colima/Jalisco coast, Saturday–Sunday (17–19 Oct); hurricane warnings and tropical storm watches issued for SW and W-central Mexico coasts
major_events.impact: Life-threatening flooding and landslides projected for Colima and Jalisco (rainfall 4–8 inches/101–203 mm); compound hazard severely elevated — Hurricane Simon’s prior rains have already saturated soils across the Guerrero–Colima corridor; Acapulco, Puerto Marqués and adjacent coastal fishing closed; region still recovering from Simon

major_events.name: SE Asian Haze / Indonesian Peatland Wildfires (Day 18+) — 4 Dead; Kuala Lumpur World’s Most Polluted Major City; Prabowo Accepts Foreign Firefighting Help
major_events.status: As of 16 Oct: Al Jazeera reports 4 deaths; AFP reports Kuala Lumpur topped IQAir global rankings, followed by Singapore and Medan; Palangkaraya (Central Kalimantan) visibility reduced to a few dozen metres; President Prabowo ordered reinforcements and approved accepting firefighting help from neighbouring countries; Indonesia officially blamed peatland degradation from food estate programmes; dense smog still blocking aerial water-bombing and cloud-seeding

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Champi — Typhoon Warning Issued for Guam and Rota (16 Oct); Rapid Intensification Underway; Damaging Winds Expected 17–18 Oct
major_events.status: Typhoon Warning issued by NWS Tiyan (Guam) at 4:11 PM ChST 16 Oct; Tropical Storm Warning for Tinian and Saipan; Flood Watch all of Guam and Northern Marianas; NWS forecasts rapid intensification to typhoon status by Saturday morning 17 Oct; expected to approach or pass directly over Guam late Saturday into Sunday 18 Oct; storm may subsequently track toward Philippines, Taiwan or Japan the following week
major_events.impact: Damaging winds expected late 17 Oct and 18 Oct; storm-total rainfall 6–12 inches (152–305 mm) creates life-threatening flash-flood risk in low-lying and urban areas; Guam still recovering from Super Typhoon Bavi (July 2026 — federal major disaster declaration issued 7 Oct)

weather.overview_html: Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified to ~90 mph on 16 October and is forecast to become a major hurricane by tonight, with landfall near Manzanillo, Colima, expected Saturday–Sunday; compound flooding and landslide risk is severe due to soils already saturated by Hurricane Simon. Simultaneously, NWS Tiyan issued a Typhoon Warning for Guam and Rota for Tropical Storm Champi, which is expected to reach typhoon intensity before landfall on Guam Sunday 18 October. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia’s wildfire haze crisis has now killed four people, with Kuala Lumpur topping IQAir’s world most-polluted-city ranking on 16 October; President Prabowo has accepted foreign firefighting aid and ordered additional resources. On the Gulf Coast, Isaias aftermath recovery continues across the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama with boil-water notices still in effect.

items.source: Yale Climate Connections / NHC / Fox10 / US News
items.headline: Hurricane Trudy Intensifies to ~90 mph on 16 Oct; Major Hurricane (Cat 3+) Forecast by Tonight; Landfall Near Manzanillo, Colima, Saturday–Sunday; Warnings Issued for SW Mexico Coast; Compound Flood Risk Severe
items.summary: Trudy reached sustained winds of approximately 90 mph (Category 1 hurricane) on October 16, an increase of roughly 20 mph since October 15 advisories, and was approximately 285 miles southwest of Acapulco moving west-northwest. The NHC forecast rapid intensification to major hurricane intensity (Category 3 or higher) by Friday evening October 16, with likely landfall near Manzanillo, Colima/Jalisco, over the weekend (October 17–19). Hurricane warnings and tropical storm watches have been issued for southwestern and west-central Mexico. Rainfall of 4–8 inches (101–203 mm) is projected for Colima and Jalisco, with life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides. The hazard is compounded by soil saturation from Hurricane Simon's prior rains across the Guerrero–Colima corridor, meaning runoff will be faster and more intense. Yale Climate Connections noted that both Trudy and Tropical Storm Champi (threatening Guam) are active simultaneously — a rare dual Eastern Pacific-Western Pacific coincidence. US News reported the storm's forecast track brings it ashore in a region with limited shelter capacity and elevated poverty levels.

items.headline: Indonesia Wildfire Haze: 4 Dead; Kuala Lumpur World’s Most Polluted Major City (16 Oct); Prabowo Accepts Foreign Aid; Singapore Weighs Transboundary Haze Act Action; Indonesia Blames Peatland Degradation
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported four deaths as Indonesia battles what multiple outlets describe as its worst forest fire season in over a decade. AFP reported on October 16 that Kuala Lumpur topped IQAir's global most-polluted major city ranking, followed by Singapore, Medan and Jakarta. In Palangkaraya, Central Kalimantan — the fire epicentre — visibility dropped to a few dozen metres. President Prabowo Subianto approved accepting firefighting assistance from neighbouring countries including Malaysia and Singapore and ordered additional ground and aerial resources; dense smog has blocked water-bombing and cloud-seeding aircraft throughout the crisis. Indonesia officially attributed the severity of the disaster to peatland degradation from government food estate programmes and pledged peat ecosystem restoration. Singapore's environment minister said the government is examining legal action under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act against Indonesian companies whose concessions are burning — a measure not used since the 2015 crisis. Schools remain closed across Malaysia and East Timor; over 1,600 domestic flights have been disrupted; hundreds of thousands have sought respiratory treatment across Central Kalimantan, South Sumatra and Papua.

items.source: NWS Tiyan (Guam) / watchers.news / cedarnews / Yale Climate Connections
items.headline: Typhoon Warning Issued for Guam and Rota (16 Oct 4:11 PM ChST): Tropical Storm Champi to Rapidly Intensify to Typhoon Before Landfall; Damaging Winds and 6–12“ Rainfall Expected 17–18 Oct; Guam Still Recovering from Super Typhoon Bavi
items.summary: NWS Tiyan issued a Typhoon Warning for Guam and Rota at 4:11 PM ChST October 16, with a Tropical Storm Warning for Tinian and Saipan and a Flood Watch for all of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. Champi is forecast to rapidly intensify to typhoon intensity by Saturday October 17 morning and to pass close to or directly over Guam late Saturday into Sunday October 18. Storm-total rainfall of 6–12 inches (152–305 mm) creates life-threatening flash flood risk, particularly in low-lying and urban areas. The storm is rated an extreme-severity event (5/5) on NWS Guam's severity scale. Guam is still recovering from Super Typhoon Bavi, which struck in July 2026; the federal government issued a major disaster declaration for Bavi on October 7. Earlier in 2026, Super Typhoon Sinlaku struck the Northern Marianas in April, causing 17 fatalities. Yale Climate Connections meteorologist Jeff Masters noted that after Guam, Champi may threaten the Philippines, Taiwan or Japan the following week. Cedar News reported a Typhoon Warning replacing the prior Typhoon Watch for Guam and Rota as the storm rapidly organised on October 16.

items.headline: Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, 105 mph) Gulf Coast Aftermath: Boil-Water Notices Persist Across Florida Panhandle; Four Dead; Recovery Ongoing from Near-Destin Landfall
items.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at approximately 8:30 pm CDT on October 10 with sustained winds of 105 mph (Category 2), killing four people and causing peak outages of approximately 900,000 customers. Power restoration had progressed significantly by October 12–13 but boil-water notices remained in effect across parts of the Florida Panhandle as of mid-week October 14–15, with water system repairs ongoing. The storm's remnants are no longer active. Florida, Alabama and Georgia are in various stages of debris removal, infrastructure repair and insurance claims processing. The storm made landfall in a region still rebuilding from prior-year hurricane impacts; FEMA pre-positioned resources in advance.

renewables.overview_html: Ørsted exercised a contractual buyback right on 12 October to acquire the remaining 49.9% of the 172 MW Gunfleet Sands 1 & 2 offshore wind farm from JERA Nex BP and the Development Bank of Japan for approximately £15 million (∼US$19.8 M); full ownership gives Ørsted flexibility to pursue a lifetime extension for the 2010-era farm. Australia’s ARENA launched Solar Sunshot Round 3 (A$250 M, EOI from 2 Nov) on 15 October and on 13 October named Round 2 awardees Built Robotics (A$14.5 M) and Luminous Robotics (A$17.8 M) for solar manufacturing facilities. In the US, the Trump administration’s Interior Department filed in federal court to rescind the operating approval for the near-complete 704 MW Revolution Wind offshore project — the third legal attempt to halt the farm, which is already delivering power to New England. In China, installed renewable capacity reached 2.496 TW by end-August 2026 (60.8% of total power capacity), with the NEA targeting 3.5 TW by 2030.

items.source: Offshore Wind Biz / RenewableWatch / OE Digital
items.headline: Ørsted Exercises Buyback Right to Acquire Remaining 49.9% of 172 MW Gunfleet Sands 1 & 2 Offshore Wind Farm for ~£15 M; Partners JERA Nex BP and DBJ Exit; Close Expected November 2026
items.summary: Ørsted announced on October 12 that it will exercise a pre-existing contractual buyback right to acquire the remaining 49.9% stake in the Gunfleet Sands 1 & 2 offshore wind farm from JERA Nex BP (24.95%) and the Development Bank of Japan (24.95%) for approximately £15 million (roughly US$19.8 million). Ørsted already holds 50.1%. The 172 MW farm sits approximately 7 km off the Essex coast and has been operational since 2010, making it one of the UK's earlier commercial offshore wind assets. Ørsted said full ownership will provide more operational flexibility and facilitate evaluation of a potential lifetime extension; no formal extension decision has been announced. Closing is subject to customary conditions and expected in November 2026. Ørsted's UK fleet of 12 offshore wind farms collectively supplies approximately 7% of UK electricity. The deal stems from provisions in the original partnership agreements and was described by Ørsted as a case-by-case assessment of similar rights in its broader portfolio.

items.headline: ARENA Solar Sunshot Round 3 Opens (A$250 M, EOI from 2 Nov); Round 2 Awards A$14.5 M to Built Robotics and A$17.8 M to Luminous Robotics for Solar Manufacturing; Round 1B Extended to 12 November
items.summary: Australia's ARENA (Australian Renewable Energy Agency) opened expressions of interest for Solar Sunshot Round 3 on October 15, allocating approximately A$250 million for advanced solar technologies, manufacturing and deployment. Expressions of interest open formally on November 2, 2026. The Solar Sunshot programme, backed by a total A$1 billion government commitment, seeks to establish an Australian solar supply chain competitive with imported modules. Separately, on October 13, ARENA named Round 2 successful applicants: US-based Built Robotics received A$14.5 million and Luminous Robotics received A$17.8 million, both to establish new solar manufacturing facilities in Australia. ARENA extended the deadline for Round 1B (upstream manufacturing feasibility studies and FEED work, A$50 million available) to November 12, 2026, to accommodate a broader applicant pool.

items.headline: Vikram Solar Secures 187 MW Solar Module Supply Order for Projects in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu; Plans Battery Storage Assembly Plant in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Indian solar module manufacturer Vikram Solar secured a 187 MW solar module supply order for utility-scale projects in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu on October 16. The company also confirmed plans to establish a battery storage assembly plant in Tamil Nadu, extending its product line beyond solar modules into energy storage — a strategic move aligned with India's accelerating battery storage procurement and its 500 GW renewable capacity target by 2030. The order adds to Vikram Solar's recent momentum in domestic and export markets; the company has previously supplied to projects in Europe, the US and Southeast Asia.

items.headline: China Renewable Capacity Reaches 2.496 TW by End-August 2026 (60.8% of Total Power Capacity); Solar 1.274 TW, Wind 679 GW; NEA Targets 3.5 TW by 2030
items.summary: China's National Energy Administration confirmed on October 14 that installed renewable power capacity reached 2.496 TW by end-August 2026 — 60.8% of the country's total installed generation capacity. Solar reached 1.274 TW, wind 679 GW and hydropower 454 GW. The pace of additions is tracking significantly ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan target of 3.5 TW by 2030, which is likely to be surpassed ahead of schedule. China's total power capacity at end-August 2026 was approximately 4.11 TW, with coal and gas together accounting for the remaining ~39%.

items.headline: Trump Administration Files in Federal Court to Rescind Revolution Wind’s Operating Approval; Project ~80% Complete and Already Delivering Power; Third Attempt to Halt the 704 MW Offshore Farm
items.summary: The US Department of the Interior filed in federal court on October 13 seeking permission to rescind the three-year-old federal operating approval for Revolution Wind, a 704 MW offshore wind farm off Connecticut and Rhode Island that has already begun delivering electricity to New England. Two prior stop-work orders were overturned by courts in 2025, which ordered construction to resume. The project is expected to reach full commercial output by end-2026. The legal action is the latest in the Trump administration's broader offshore wind rollback, which has paused or challenged federal approvals for five offshore projects. Developers Ørsted and Eversource have not publicly commented on the latest filing.

items.headline: PNE AG Cuts 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance ~40% (New Range: €65–80 M vs. Prior €110–140 M); Wind Project Sale Delays and Permitting Backlogs Cited; Some 2026 Revenue Shifts to 2027
items.summary: German SDax-listed wind park developer PNE AG issued a significant earnings guidance cut on October 14, reducing its 2026 adjusted EBITDA forecast to €65–80 million from the prior range of €110–140 million — a reduction of approximately 40% at midpoint. The company cited delays in planned wind park project sales, delayed permitting approvals, and a strategic decision to retain some operating wind parks rather than sell them. Revenue expected in 2026 will now shift into 2027. The guidance cut reflects the continuing difficulty of the German wind development market, where approval procedures have lengthened significantly despite recent regulatory reform efforts.

items.headline: Fingrid (Finland) Mandates Grid-Forming Capability for New Large-Scale Wind and Solar in Converter-Dominated Grid Regions; Requirements Published 15 October 2026
items.summary: Finnish TSO Fingrid published mandatory technical requirements on October 15 obliging new large-scale wind and solar plants connected in converter-dominated portions of its network to provide grid-forming control. The requirements address a growing stability risk: converter-connected generation was supplying roughly 65% of Finland's system power at peak times in 2026. Grid-following inverters — the current standard for renewable installations — require synchronous generation to maintain stable voltage and frequency; without grid-forming capability, adding more converter-based capacity in weak grid areas risks instability. Fingrid already operates synchronous condensers and a STATCOM; the new requirements shift cost and responsibility to project developers. Finland had approximately 8,885 MW of installed wind and around 1,500 MW of solar as of mid-2026.

science.overview_html: The week’s science picture is dominated by the Copernicus C3S September 2026 bulletin confirming the Niño 3.4 region has set an all-time monthly SST record (+3.34°C anomaly) and the extra-polar ocean hit a September record of 21.05°C, with Carbon Brief describing the 2026 Super El Niño as reaching a “remarkable” all-time record that is expected to have its greatest surface-temperature impact in early 2027. In AI-for-weather, ECMWF’s science blog on the AI Weather Quest 2026 reported that roughly half of the 39 submitted models are purely data-driven, and that probabilistic debiasing has emerged as the key differentiator for subseasonal skill — confirming the Microsoft Research / MIT Nature paper published 14 October as the standout methodological advance of the period. Berkeley Earth now places the probability of 2026 finishing as the hottest year on record at 93%.

items.headline: Copernicus C3S September 2026: Niño 3.4 Sets All-Time Monthly SST Record; Extra-Polar Ocean Reaches Record 21.05°C; 2nd Warmest September (1.63°C Above Pre-Industrial); Antarctic Sea Ice Third-Lowest Winter Maximum
items.meta: Copernicus Climate Change Service · Monthly Climate Bulletin, October 2026
items.summary: The Copernicus C3S October 2026 bulletin's headline oceanographic finding is an all-time monthly SST record for the Niño 3.4 region of the central equatorial Pacific, exceeding the peak of the 2015–16 event across all available data. The extra-polar ocean average (60°S–60°N) reached 21.05°C — a September record. Global mean surface air temperature was 16.27°C, placing September 2026 as the second-warmest September in the ERA5 record (0.11°C below September 2023). Both August and September 2026 registered global temperatures exceeding 1.5°C above the 1850–1900 pre-industrial baseline: 1.63°C for September. Antarctic sea ice reached its third-lowest annual winter maximum extent. In the atmosphere, dry conditions intensified or expanded across Iberia, France, Italy, the western Balkans and Greece; Western Europe tied its warmest September on record. The bulletin provides the primary scientific data underpinning current assessments that 2026 may become the hottest year on record, with a larger temperature impact from the El Niño signal expected in 2027.

items.headline: Carbon Brief Analysis: 2026 Super El Niño Reaches “Remarkable” All-Time Niño 3.4 Anomaly Record (+3.34°C); Peak Global Temperature Impact Expected in Early 2027; 2026 Annual Mean Likely 1.536–1.642°C Above Pre-Industrial Baseline
items.summary: Carbon Brief's October 13 analysis describes the 2026 El Niño as having reached a 'remarkable' all-time record for the Niño 3.4 SST anomaly (+3.34°C), exceeding the peaks of all previous strong El Niños in the instrumental record including 2015–16. Copernicus director Carlo Buontempo stated 2026 could still become the hottest year ever recorded, though this depends on October–December conditions. Carbon Brief notes that El Niño's peak impact on global surface air temperatures typically lags the SST peak by 3–6 months; accordingly the largest warming boost to the global mean is projected for early 2027. A Berkeley Earth assessment (August 2026) placed the probability of 2026 breaking the annual record at 93%, with the likely annual global mean between 1.536 and 1.642°C above the 1850–1900 baseline. Carbon Brief projects 2027 at approximately 1.7°C above pre-industrial — which, if confirmed, would represent the most sustained exceedance of the 1.5°C Paris threshold yet recorded.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of the Climate (Oct 2026): 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest or Warmest Year on Record; Berkeley Earth at 93% Probability; Carbon Brief Central Estimate ~1.51°C Above Pre-Industrial; 2027 Projected at ~1.7°C
items.meta: Carbon Brief · State of the Climate, 13 October 2026
items.summary: Carbon Brief's monthly State of the Climate update for October 2026 placed the year's likely annual average temperature at approximately 1.51°C above pre-industrial levels, with a central estimate making 2026 the second-warmest year on record and a 35% probability it surpasses 2024 to set a new annual record. Berkeley Earth's August 2026 assessment was substantially more bullish at 93% probability, with the likely annual mean between 1.536 and 1.642°C above the 1850–1900 baseline. The different probabilities reflect methodology and the data period used: Carbon Brief draws on ERA5/HadCRUT and uses a conservative baseline-comparison approach, while Berkeley Earth uses a running-mean methodology more sensitive to recent SST anomalies. Both analyses agree 2027 is projected to be the warmest year on record, with the El Niño's surface temperature signal peaking after the SST maximum. Carbon Brief projects 2027 at approximately 1.7°C above pre-industrial, and noted that sustained 1.5°C exceedance over 1–2 decades is the threshold that most climate scientists regard as a meaningful breach of the Paris goal.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest 2026 Science Blog: Half of 39 Submitted Models Are Purely Data-Driven; Probabilistic Debiasing Emerges as Critical Differentiator for Subseasonal Skill; MicroDuet Leads All Variables and Lead Times
items.summary: ECMWF's science blog on the AI Weather Quest competition — the first public S2S prediction competition organised under the WMO Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Prediction Project — reported that roughly half of the 39 models submitted across the first two competition periods are purely data-driven AI systems, with the remainder being postprocessing methods or hybrid physics-AI systems. MicroDuet (Microsoft Research and MIT) leads all weather variables and lead times. The blog's institutional assessment highlighted probabilistic debiasing as now the critical bottleneck for AI model utility at the 2–6 week range, rather than the choice of base architecture: the ECMWF noted that AI models trained on raw ensemble output systematically under-represent uncertainty at S2S timescales, and that the Microsoft Research/MIT Nature paper (arXiv:2604.16238) demonstrated that all six major operational forecasting centres' models show negative precipitation skill at S2S ranges without such correction. The competition is structured to reward calibrated probabilistic forecasts, accelerating adoption of bias-correction methods across the community.

items.title: CarbonFarm Raises €7 M (∼US$7.8 M) Series A to Scale AI-Assisted Methane MRV for Rice Cultivation Globally; >100,000 Ha Deployed Across 8+ Countries
items.body_html: CarbonFarm, a Paris-based startup using satellite data and AI to measure, report and verify methane reductions from rice farming, closed an oversubscribed €7 million (approximately US$7.8 M) Series A round on 13 October 2026. The round was led by Colam Impact, with Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo and BPI France also participating; existing backers Serena & makesense (Racine²) and Techmind renewed. The company’s MRV platform covers more than 100,000 hectares in 8+ countries; its credits are accepted in most regulated carbon markets. Rice cultivation produces approximately 12% of human-caused methane and uses up to 28% of global freshwater; improved water management can cut rice methane emissions by up to 50%. Funds will support digital MRV expansion and new project development across Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America.

items.title: Moody’s RMS Launches Australia Cyclone and Flood HD Model: First Combined Tropical Cyclone Wind, Storm-Surge and Inland-Flood High-Definition Catastrophe Model for the Australian Market
items.body_html: Moody’s RMS introduced the Australia Cyclone and Flood HD Model on 6 October 2026, the first catastrophe model to combine tropical cyclone wind, storm-surge flood and inland rainfall-flood into a single high-definition framework for the Australian market. The rationale is that cyclone and flood are underwritten together and jointly reinsured through the Australian government-backed Cyclone Reinsurance Pool; modelling them in isolation understates compound event loss. Tropical Cyclone Alfred (2025) — which produced major flood losses after winds eased — was cited as the motivating example. The model is designed for insurers and reinsurers active in the Australian ICA-classified cyclone-prone regions, where cyclones account for over a quarter of insured natural catastrophe losses. Moody’s has signalled a plan to complete a fully consistent Australian multi-peril suite, including bushfire.

items.title: Wildfire-Exposed Catastrophe Bond Issuance Reaches US$5.183 Billion YTD in 2026, Approaching Full-Year Record; Insurers Transfer Record Climate-Linked Risk to Capital Markets
items.body_html: Wildfire-exposed catastrophe bond issuance has reached US$5.183 billion year-to-date in 2026, according to Artemis.bm, rapidly approaching the full-year record of US$5.55 billion set in 2025. The surge reflects insurers and reinsurers accelerating use of the capital markets to transfer wildfire risk, driven by escalating insured losses across California, the Mountain West and Southern Europe. The broader ILS market hit a record outstanding of approximately US$65.6 billion in mid-2026. The growth trajectory for wildfire-linked paper aligns with vendor model updates from Verisk and Moody’s that now incorporate climate-adjusted hazard frequencies and changing fire behaviour, raising modelled annual expected losses for wildfire perils.

items.title: TWIA Forecasts US$2.05 Billion Reinsurance and Cat Bond Need for 2027, Proposes 18% Budget Reduction
items.body_html: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association (TWIA) has forecast a US$2.05 billion reinsurance and catastrophe bond requirement for its 2027 programme, according to Artemis.bm on 7 October. The forecast accompanies a proposed 18% budget reduction, reflecting continued tightening of TWIA’s exposure management and shifting reinsurance market conditions. TWIA insures properties in the high-risk Gulf Coast counties of Texas that the private market will not cover; its reinsurance tower is one of the largest state wind-pool programmes in the US. The 2027 programme will be informed by updated vendor catastrophe model loss estimates and current ILS market pricing, which has seen the global cat bond market reach a record ~US$65.6 billion outstanding in mid-2026.
